subsystems.name: Market model
subsystems.role: describes how an asset, rate or portfolio value can move over the contract's life.
parts: stochastic process (e.g. geometric Brownian motion, Heston)
discretisation grid in time and value

subsystems.name: State preparation
subsystems.role: loads that probability distribution into the amplitudes of a quantum register, so measuring returns a value with the right odds.
parts: piecewise or polynomial approximation of the distribution

subsystems.name: Objective oracle
subsystems.role: computes the quantity whose expectation is wanted — a payoff, a loss threshold, a portfolio value.

subsystems.name: Amplitude estimation core
subsystems.role: extracts the expectation with quadratically fewer samples than classical Monte Carlo.
parts: quantum phase estimation, or low-depth variants (iterative and maximum-likelihood amplitude estimation)

subsystems.name: Quantum processor
subsystems.role: runs the circuit — today a noisy machine, eventually an error-corrected one.

subsystems.name: Classical orchestration
subsystems.role: compiles the circuit, calibrates it, runs repeated shots and turns the counts into a price with an error bar.

buildSteps.title: Fix the financial question
buildSteps.detail: Choose the contract or risk measure, e.g. the expected discounted payoff of a European or path-dependent option over a set horizon.

buildSteps.title: Discretise the model
buildSteps.detail: Approximate the continuous stochastic process on a grid of time steps and values, giving a finite distribution over N = 2^n outcomes.

buildSteps.title: Load the distribution
buildSteps.detail: Build operator A that maps a register of all-zero qubits to amplitudes whose squares equal the discretised probabilities.

buildSteps.title: Build the payoff circuit
buildSteps.detail: Implement the payoff as reversible arithmetic: add, multiply and compare, writing a flag qubit that marks favourable outcomes.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the Grover operator
buildSteps.detail: Combine A with reflections about the zero state and about the marked subspace to form Q = A S₀ A† S_χ, which rotates the state by a fixed angle each application.

buildSteps.title: Estimate the amplitude
buildSteps.detail: Apply phase estimation to Q (or use iterative / maximum-likelihood variants that need fewer qubits) and read off the angle, which encodes the expectation to precision 1/N rather than 1/√N.

buildSteps.title: Run and mitigate
buildSteps.detail: Execute on real hardware, applying error mitigation and measuring many shots; compare the result and its uncertainty against classical Monte Carlo.

buildSteps.title: Scale to production
buildSteps.detail: Repeat on error-corrected hardware, embedding the routine inside the bank's existing pricing and risk pipelines.

prerequisites.why: payoff circuits and phase estimation need far more qubits and far deeper circuits than today's noisy devices can hold.
loading an arbitrary distribution is a major cost; only small, specially structured distributions have been prepared so far.
adders and comparators exist and are tested, but at the size needed for realistic payoffs they are still impractical.
iterative and maximum-likelihood amplitude estimation trade qubits for repetitions, making near-term runs possible at reduced precision.

prerequisites.tech: Classical Monte Carlo and market models
prerequisites.why: they provide the benchmarks any quantum result must beat, and the risk systems it would eventually plug into.

pathway.milestone: proof-of-concept runs on small noisy devices, computing option prices or credit-risk measures for simplified models
pathway.unlocks: practical know-how about circuit depth, state preparation and error mitigation in a financial setting.

pathway.milestone: end-to-end resource estimates for realistic contracts on early error-corrected machines
pathway.unlocks: a clear target for hardware roadmaps and for deciding which financial problems are worth attacking first.

pathway.milestone: a controlled demonstration that beats classical Monte Carlo on a task a bank actually cares about
pathway.unlocks: the first genuine commercial pilots inside pricing and risk desks.

pathway.milestone: advantage at production scale across portfolios, not just single contracts
pathway.unlocks: faster risk aggregation, more accurate pricing of complex derivatives, and better capital allocation.
